is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles gambiae (s.s.) females collected in western Kenya (Methods, p. 1 and p. 7-8).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study solely genotypes the 2La chromosomal inversion using PCR breakpoints. The target resistance marker Vgsc L1014S (L995S) is discussed only by reference to previous published work (Mathias et al. 2011, ref [22]) and was not genotyped in this study (p. 3, 5, 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts or frequencies are reported for any of the target insecticide resistance markers.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were field-collected from Asembo and Seme in western Kenya between 1994 and 2011 (p. 1, 7).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary research article reporting original 2La inversion PCR assays on banked and fresh mosquito specimens.

sub_country_location.evidence: Asembo (Rarieda sub-County, Siaya County) and Seme (Seme sub-County, Kisumu County), Kenya (p. 7).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Individual collection years are reported: 1994, 1996, 2000, 2005, 2008, 2009, and 2011 (Table 1, p. 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Banked specimens from earlier collection protocols described in Bayoh et al. 2010 were tested, but for 2La karyotyping.

supplement.evidence: All relevant data from the paper are contained in the main text; no supplementary files are needed.

assessment.summary: This study analyzes the temporal decline in the frequency of the 2La chromosomal inversion in Anopheles gambiae (s.s.) from Asembo and Seme in western Kenya between 1994 and 2011 in relation to ITN ownership. No target insecticide resistance markers were genotyped.
